request.spec:
Show for the sheet the due of OPEN and PENDING claims that count by age, as the people's age
buckets added up (0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 or more days), not trimmed.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show for the sheet the due of OPEN and PENDING claims that count by age, as the people's age
buckets added up (0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 or more days), not trimmed.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now shows its total due by claim age, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

Three new figures sit with the other sheet totals (claimed, due, settled, open, overdue, cuts). They show the due of OPEN and PENDING claims that count, split into the same age buckets as each person's row: 0 to 30, 31 to 60, and 61 or more days. Each is every person's bucket added up, with no trimming, using the test's `rollup-aged-0-30`, `rollup-aged-31-60` and `rollup-aged-61` ids.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. I split the per-person age calculation so the row display and the new sheet totals use the same numbers. Nothing changed on the server or in the stored data, because the screen already loads everything it needs. The other sheet totals are worked out on the screen the same way.
